candidate.title: EpiRADseq
candidate.scope: The middle EpiRADseq row of the supplied Illumina poster crop, from genomic DNA and restriction sites through the amplified DNA library. The neighboring Methyl-Seq/MRE-Seq and T-WGBS rows are separate workflows. ddRADseq is named as the architectural basis within the EpiRADseq description, not as an alternative target. This graph preserves the diagram-local sequence; the primary-supported correction explicitly distinguishes the published EpiRADseq digestion-before-ligation order. Sequencing readout is interpreted from the paper without adding unshown sequencing or computational operations.

states.label: Genome / Restriction sites
features: Genomic DNA is shown as a blue line, first with a yellow-highlighted region and then with marked restriction sites; these are explanatory views of the substrate, not two demonstrated processing steps.
The biological target is variation in cytosine methylation at assayable restriction sites, rather than all methylated bases throughout the genome.

states.label: DNA: amplified reduced-representation library
features: The diagram ends at a stack of blue DNA lines after Amplify; it does not draw a sequencing or analysis operation in the EpiRADseq row.

Amplified genomic fragments are the sequencing-library carrier. Their locus sequence identifies the sampled restriction-associated region; barcoded adapters associate recovered fragments with samples.

When sequenced, relative recovery and read depth at sampled CCGG-associated loci report the frequency of cuttable, unmethylated templates. This is a reduced representation, not a base-by-base map of all genomic methylation.
The final icon omits adapter colors; that simplification is not evidence of adapter removal.
Locus recovery is averaged across sampled cells and DNA strands; this readout does not distinguish homo-methylation from hemi-methylation or identify which cells carry the mark.

Restriction-site genotype differences can change locus recovery independently of methylation. Read absence or reduced depth alone therefore does not prove methylation in genetically different samples.

operations.label: Second restriction digest with methylation-sensitive HpaII
operations.description: In the diagram, the already barcoded long fragments are cleaved into shorter fragments with a new end available for P2 addition. This local input history and drawn route are retained. For the actual Schield EpiRADseq implementation, the primary-supported order is PstI/HpaII digestion before adapter ligation; this diagram-local placement must not be treated as the published protocol order.
operations.mechanism: HpaII recognizes CCGG; methylation of its relevant cut site prevents cleavage and hence recovery of the corresponding EpiRADseq locus. The figure does not show a separate retained methylated/uncut branch.
operations.information_effect: Methylation-sensitive cutting changes which genomic loci can enter the recoverable library; methylation is represented through locus recovery frequency, not a converted base in the sequencing read.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operations belong to the single EpiRADseq row. The title and row descriptor identify double-digest restriction site-associated DNA marker generation with a methylation-sensitive restriction enzyme. Neither the adjacent rows nor the paper-discussed MspI/ddRADseq genotype-control extension is a depicted alternative target. The primary paper supports EpiRADseq and resolves the implementation order: both restriction enzymes precede ligation; the drawing remains a separate schematic depiction, not evidence for interchangeable complete implementations.
